title: You thought God abandoned you…
paragraphs:
You thought God abandoned you…
But what if He was exposing you?
Because the fire didn’t just burn your situation.

It revealed something in you
you didn’t want to see.

You prayed for peace…
but your life got louder.

You asked for blessing…
but everything started breaking.
And deep inside, a question started whispering:
“God… why are You doing this to me?”
Let me answer you with trembling truth:

What if God isn’t attacking you—
He’s uncovering you?
Because we love a God who comforts…
But we resist a God who tests.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable:
Some of what you’re feeling right now?

That pressure.
That exposure.
That internal shaking.
It’s not even just the enemy.

It’s God putting His finger
on the parts of your heart
you kept hidden—even from yourself.

“For You, O God, have tested us;
You have refined us as silver is refined.” — Psalm 66:10
Silver doesn’t become pure in comfort.

That anger you justified?
That secret habit you renamed?
That pride you called “confidence”?
Now it’s all rising to the surface.
Here’s the truth most people don’t preach:
God will expose what He intends to heal.

“The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold,
but the Lord tests the heart.” — Proverbs 17:3
You can say all the right things…

He will allow pressure
just to show you
what’s really ruling you.
This is where shame tries to take over.

“Look at you.”
“You’re still like this?”
“After everything God has done?”
The other keeps you from Him.
Now listen carefully—this is the turning point:

God is not exposing you to shame you.
He’s exposing you to save you.
Before this moment of raw honesty…
Jesus already stepped into the ultimate fire for you.
On that cross, Jesus didn’t just carry your visible sins.

The ones you manage.
The ones you excuse.
The ones no one knows.
So now, when God refines you—
You are being purified without being condemned.

Some scholars interpret trials like these as both discipline and preparation—
not to earn God’s love, but to shape us for His purpose.
Because salvation is not behavior management.

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us
and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
So what do you do when the fire hits?

You bring the real you
to the real Jesus.
Because grace doesn’t meet you where you pretend to be.
It meets you where you actually are.
And here’s the promise that holds you steady in the heat:

“After you have suffered a little while,
He will restore, confirm, strengthen, and establish you.” — 1 Peter 5:10
This fire has an expiration date.
Let God finish what He started in you.
What is God trying to purify?
What have I been avoiding that God is now confronting?
Whisper this if you mean it:

“Lord, search me.
Not my comfort—my heart.
Expose what’s not like You.
And give me the courage to surrender it.”
This is not just a post.
You’ll need it when the fire feels too much.
If this stirred something in you…
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
